applies_why: This judge text decides a collision between the challenger's seed/loins chain and the defender's chain, so it is the chain-against-chain situation K-C governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — reading one: the judge may fault a footed chain for lacking an explicit Joseph naming; reading two: K-C forbids such verse-level naming demands and requires only chain-footing.
why: The judge treats a footed chain as underdetermined because it does not explicitly name Joseph, imposing a verse-level stating requirement that K-C's chain-against-chain footing test bars.
